messages:
Priya (Product): Quick sync on scorecard keyboard shortcuts & bulk approval modal. Idea: j/k to move, space to expand diff, A to approve single, Shift+A for bulk. Want to speed up reviewer throughput.

Ethan (Design): Strong +1. UX considerations: show a small keyhint pill when list focused (e.g., 'j k • space • A'). Also avoid using letters that conflict with browser/OS combos. Maybe require list focus to enable shortcuts.

Raj (Engineering): We'll gate shortcuts behind list focus. Technical caveats: virtualized lists mean 'next' should only consider rendered rows. Also for A/Shift+A we should present a confirmation modal for bulk actions.

Mei (Research): Power users like this. For discoverability, add a "Keyboard shortcuts" link in the scorecard header and surface the command palette (Cmd/Ctrl+K) option. Run an A/B to measure adoption.

Jules (Accessibility): A11y checklist:
- Add aria-keyshortcuts attributes where possible (note: support varies across AT).
- When a diff opens, move focus into it and trap until Escape collapses it and returns focus to the row.
- Use ARIA live region to announce "Diff opened for <prompt set>" and "N of M diffs" when navigating.
- Prefer modifier combos (e.g., Ctrl/Alt) for reliability over shifted letters for some assistive tech.

Nora (QA): Test cases I plan to add:
- j/k navigate visible rows only (virtual list)
- space toggles diff + focus trap + Escape behavior
- A opens confirm modal with correct count and details
- Shift+A triggers bulk modal with preview and requires explicit approve click
- Shortcuts disabled while search or inline-edit input is focused
- Live region announcements happen on open/close
Also catch: accidental double-approve when users mash keys. We'll add debounce & server-side idempotency.

Priya (Product): Modal copy question: header "Approve 8 items" vs "Confirm approval" vs "Approve for rollout". I want clarity for reviewers.

Ethan (Design): Recommend "Approve 8 prompt tests" as header + subtext: "This marks the selected tests as approved for rollout." Primary button label: "Approve". Secondary: "Cancel". Keep it short and explicit.

Jules (Accessibility): Ensure modal has aria-describedby pointing to the subtext. After success, announce via live region "8 tests approved". Also ensure focus management: focus the primary action by default but allow keyboard users to cancel quickly.

Raj (Engineering): Backend: approval endpoint returns job id; large batches process async. UI should show toast "Approvals processing (8)" and per-row pending state. We'll implement client-side 800ms debounce to prevent duplicate submits and server-side dedupe by user+batch id. Also provide an undo window (10s) that calls a revert endpoint.

Mei (Research): Suggest A/B: Variant A surfaces shortcut pill + command palette; Variant B shows one-time tooltip explaining shortcuts. Metrics: time-to-approve, #approvals per session, undo rate. Run for 10k sessions or 2 weeks.

Nora (QA): I'll add automation for the shortcut flows and the modal regressions, and include a flaky test guard for virtual list timing.

Priya (Product): Action items:
- Ethan: mock keyhint pill, modal copy, and header UI (Figma link) by Wed.
- Raj: implement keyboard handlers, debounce, server-side idempotency, undo API (PR target next Fri).
- Jules: provide exact ARIA props + live region copy by Tue.
- Nora: add regression tests and automation plan by Thu.
- Mei: draft A/B test plan and metrics by Mon.

Ethan (Design): Tiny visual nit: when diff pane animates open, ensure reduced-motion respects user OS prefs and provide an instant state for reduced-motion.

Jules (Accessibility): Good call. Reduced-motion is critical. Also ensure color contrast for keyhint pill meets 4.5:1.

Raj (Engineering): Noted. We'll respect prefers-reduced-motion and use CSS variables for pill color so contrast can be tweaked.

Priya (Product): Great. I'll file the ticket with acceptance criteria and link to Figma once Ethan uploads mocks. Thanks team :sparkles:
